LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING A REPLY TO A FRIENDLY LETTER

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing A Reply to a Friendly Letter
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing A Reply to a Friendly Letter, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How do you communicate with people who are far away? 2. Why do we write letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing A Reply to a Friendly Letter together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: Learning independently as learners, individually, write a reply to a sample friendly letter using the correct format.

• Creativity and Imagination: Originality as learners compose friendly letters

Values:
Love: Sharing as learner proofread each other’s work and edit the letter reads

Link to other Subjects:

Learners are able to relate the skill of letter writing to their learning in Kiswahili.
